output_text: <laravel-boost-guidelines>Follow Laravel Boost guidelines for this Laravel app; it is curated by Laravel maintainers. This application is a Laravel app and its main Laravel ecosystem package & versions are: inertiajs/inertia-laravel v2; laravel/fortify v1; laravel/framework v12; laravel/prompts v0; laravel/wayfinder v0; laravel/boost v2; laravel/mcp v0; laravel/pail v1; laravel/pint v1; laravel/sail v1; pestphp/pest v4; phpunit/phpunit v12. You MUST activate relevant skill whenever working in that domain. Activate `wayfinder-development` whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components; use when importing from @/actions or @/routes, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or working with Wayfinder route functions. Activate `pest-testing` when writing tests, creating unit/feature tests, adding assertions, testing Livewire components, browser testing, debugging test failures, working with datasets or mocking; or when user mentions test/spec/TDD/expect/asssertion/coverage/needs to verify functionality works. Follow all existing code conventions; when creating/editing a file, check sibling files for correct structure/approach/naming. Use descriptive names for variables/methods (e.g., `isRegisteredForDiscounts`). Check for existing components to reuse before writing new one. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work; unit/feature tests are more important. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. If user doesn't see a frontend change reflected in UI, it could mean they need to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise in explanations. Laravel Boost is an MCP server; use its tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` when you need to call an Artisan command to double-check available parameters. Whenever you share a project URL, use `get-absolute-url`. You should use `tinker` to execute PHP for debugging or querying Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` when only reading from database. Use `database-schema` to inspect table structure before writing migrations/models. Read browser logs/errors/exceptions using `browser-logs` (only recent logs). Boost `search-docs` must be used before other approaches when working with Laravel/Laravel ecosystem packages; it automatically passes installed packages+versions and returns only version-specific docs for the user's circumstance; filter with a packages array if needed. Search docs before making code changes. Use multiple broad simple topic-based queries at once (e.g., `['rate limiting','routing rate limiting','routing']`), and do not add package names to queries. Use these search query patterns: 1) query=authentication; 2) query=rate limit; 3) query="infinite scroll"; 4) query=middleware "rate limit" - "middleware" AND exact phrase; 5) queries=["authentication","middleware"] - ANY terms. Use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`: `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods/functions; include PHP type hints for parameters. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments; never use comments within code unless logic exceptionally complex. Add useful array shape type definitions when appropriate. Typically keys in enums should be TitleCase. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. The app served by Laravel Herd and is available at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`; use `get-absolute-url` tool to generate valid URLs. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd. Every change must be programmatically tested: write a new test or update existing test, then run affected tests to ensure they pass. Run minimum number of tests needed; use `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename/filter. Inertia rules: Inertia creates fully client-side rendered SPAs without modern SPA complexity; leverage server-side patterns. Components live in `resources/js/pages` (unless specified in `vite.config.js`). Use `Inertia::render()` for server-side routing instead of Blade views. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia docs and updated code examples. Inertia v2 rules: use all v1+v2 features; check docs before changes. New features: deferred props, infinite scrolling (merging props + `WhenVisible`), lazy loading on scroll, polling, prefetching. When using deferred props, add an empty state with a pulsing/animated skeleton. Laravel core rules: Use `php artisan make:` commands for new files (migrations/controllers/models/etc.); list available Artisan commands via `list-artisan-commands`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands; pass correct `--options`. Use proper Eloquent relationship methods with return type hints; prefer relationships over raw queries/manual joins. Use Eloquent models/relationships before suggesting raw database queries. Avoid `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`. Prevent N+1 via eager loading. Use query builder for very complex DB operations. When creating new models, create useful factories and seeders too; ask user if they need other things and use `list-artisan-commands` to check options for `php artisan make:model`. For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and API versioning unless existing API routes differ; follow existing convention. Always create Form Request classes for validation rather than inline validation in controllers; include validation rules and custom error messages. Check sibling Form Requests for array vs string based rules. Use Laravel auth/authorization features (gates/policies/Sanctum/etc.). When generating links, prefer named routes and `route()`. Use queued jobs for time-consuming operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in config files—never use `env()` directly outside config files; always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. For tests/models, use factories; check factory custom states before manually setting up model. Faker: use `$this->faker->word()` or `fake()->randomDigit()`; follow existing conventions. Creating tests: use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}` for feature tests; pass `--unit` for unit tests; most tests should be feature tests. If you see `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, run `npm run build` or ask user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Laravel docs. Laravel 11 streamlined file structure used.
